bloodlust.label: Bloodlust
bloodlust.definition: An informal name for combat-damage triggers that grow a creature with +1/+1 counters after it hits a player. It is distinct from the Bloodthirst keyword.

bloodlust.example: A creature must actually deal the specified combat damage to the required player. Evasion can help it connect; counter amplification needs a real counter event. Read whether the effect grows itself or other creatures.

saboteur.label: Saboteur
saboteur.definition: A nickname for a creature rewarded when it deals combat damage to a player. The reward can be cards, counters or another effect; it is not one keyword.

slith.label: Slith
slith.definition: A creature subtype associated with Mirrodin. “Slith ability” is also an informal nickname for combat-hit counter growth, but the subtype and that ability are separate properties.

evasion.label: Evasion
evasion.definition: Abilities that make an attacking creature harder to block help combat-hit plans connect. Flying and menace impose different blocking restrictions.

evasion.title: Evasion in play

aristocrats.label: Aristocrats
aristocrats.definition: A sacrifice-focused plan converts expendable creatures or other permanents into value through outlets and rewards for sacrificing or dying.
aristocrats.tip: Explanation and search vocabulary only. This entry does not certify a complete strategy or a working interaction.
aristocrats.title: Aristocrats in play
aristocrats.example: Provide expendable material, a usable sacrifice outlet and a payoff. A sacrifice outlet does not automatically create replacement material or an infinite loop.

blink.label: Blink / flicker
blink.definition: Exile-and-return effects can reuse enter-the-battlefield abilities or protect a permanent. Each effect specifies what returns, when it returns and who controls it.

voltron.label: Voltron
voltron.definition: A plan that concentrates enhancements on one attacking creature, often a commander, using Equipment, Auras, counters or combat tricks.

ramp.label: Mana acceleration
ramp.definition: A resource plan increases available mana so larger or additional plays become possible. Extra lands, mana permanents and temporary mana have different limits.

cantrip.label: Cantrip
cantrip.definition: A spell that draws a replacement card alongside its other effect is commonly called a cantrip. Replacing itself is different from generating extra cards.

looting.label: Looting
looting.definition: Draw-then-discard selection changes the cards in hand without necessarily increasing their number. The order matters when comparing it with discard-then-draw effects.

tutor.label: Tutor
tutor.definition: A search effect finds a card from the library according to its restrictions. Its destination and visibility are determined by the individual effect.

mtg-traditional.label: Traditional foil
mtg-traditional.note: Foil under the whole card; inks tint it, dark ink absorbs it. A broad diagonal rainbow rolls across as you tilt.

mtg-oldborder.label: Old-border foil
mtg-oldborder.note: Wider, hazier, more saturated band, with the shooting-star foil mark in the rules box.

mtg-ftv.label: From the Vault foil
mtg-ftv.note: Hyper-glossy laminate: a sharp vertical mirror bar sweeps left to right.

mtg-etched.label: Foil-etched
mtg-etched.note: Art printed on white; the frame is frosted metal grain that sparkles instead of mirroring.

mtg-etched-full.label: Foil-etched (borderless)
mtg-etched-full.note: Borderless etched cards have no frame: the frosted metal grain runs across the whole face, art included.

mtg-textured.label: Textured foil
mtg-textured.note: Fine raised grooves follow the artwork's own contours, so light ripples around the drawing while the art and text stay clear.

mtg-surge.label: Surge foil
mtg-surge.note: Crossing wave fields and sparks; bands surge in different directions.

mtg-galaxy.label: Galaxy foil
mtg-galaxy.note: Traditional foil with a field of star points that twinkle on and off.

mtg-halo.label: Halo foil
mtg-halo.note: A swirling halo pattern: rainbow arcs wheel around the centre.

mtg-confetti.label: Confetti foil
mtg-confetti.note: Scattered confetti pieces, each with its own angle, flash independently.

mtg-doublerainbow.label: Double rainbow foil
mtg-doublerainbow.note: Two crossed gratings: two rainbows at once, the brightest standard pattern.

mtg-fracture.label: Fracture foil
mtg-fracture.note: Broken-glass panels; seams catch the light as a panel turns.

mtg-ripple.label: Ripple foil
mtg-ripple.note: Concentric ripples spreading from the centre.

mtg-mana.label: Mana foil
mtg-mana.note: Mana-symbol rings pressed into the foil.

mtg-dragonscale.label: Dragonscale foil
mtg-dragonscale.note: Overlapping scales, each catching the light at its own angle.

mtg-rainbow.label: Rainbow foil
mtg-rainbow.note: Fine, high-dispersion lines: saturated rainbow at almost every angle.

mtg-invisible.label: Invisible ink
mtg-invisible.note: A hidden pattern only appears in the reflection.

mtg-raised.label: Raised foil
mtg-raised.note: Traditional foil with raised, glossy drawn lines.

mtg-oilslick.label: Oil slick foil
mtg-oilslick.note: Black card; only the raised drawn lines are glossy, with thin-film oil colours.

mtg-compleat.label: Step-and-compleat foil
mtg-compleat.note: Foil only where the sketch leaves bare paper; the ink lines stay matte.

mtg-gilded.label: Gilded foil
mtg-gilded.note: Raised gold foil on the gold ink only; the rest is matte.

mtg-neon.label: Neon ink foil
mtg-neon.note: Fluorescent ink glows over the foil; neon parts stay vivid even unlit.

mtg-silver.label: Silver foil
mtg-silver.note: Achromatic silver mirror with only a hint of colour.

mtg-firstplace.label: First-place foil
mtg-firstplace.note: A gold-plated mirror sheet across the whole card.

mtg-masterpiece.label: Masterpiece foil
mtg-masterpiece.note: Zendikar Expeditions, Kaladesh Inventions, Amonkhet Invocations: a high-gloss mirror finish.

mtg-ampersand.label: Ampersand foil
mtg-ampersand.note: Traditional foil with a large glossy D&D ampersand stamped across the card (approximate shape).

mtg-silverscreen.label: Silver screen foil
mtg-silverscreen.note: Black-and-white film look: a silver nitrate sheen over the monochrome art.

mtg-scroll.label: Scroll foil
mtg-scroll.note: Parchment-matte ink; only the paper areas take a liquid-silver sheen.

mtg-vaultboy.label: Vault Boy foil
mtg-vaultboy.note: Fallout Pip-Boy screen: CRT scanlines rolling through the foil.

mtg-pds.label: Premium Deck foil
mtg-pds.note: Premium Deck Series: a softer version of the From the Vault mirror bar.

mtg-emblem.label: Set emblem foil
mtg-emblem.note: A set's own emblem pressed into the foil (approximate shape).
